text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 tail latency spike + streaming stalls for prod /v1/stream (eu-west2). SLO breach started ~ 3501234550. Alert: p99=3.4s (baseline 420ms), streaming stall rate 6.2% (target <0.5%).

tim_oncall: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking dashboards. any customer-facing pages? @maria_support?

maria_support: getting customer list now. two high-touch customers on dedicated capacity are seeing degraded responses; support ticket numbers TKT-4821, TKT-4822. customers reporting repeated reconnects during streaming.

asha_sre: initial look — metrics show spike coincident with increased TCP/TLS handshake durations from nodes in az-b -> az-c cross-zone path. Packet retransmit rate up ~1.8% (normal <0.2). NAT ephemeral port exhaustion? checking NAT gw metrics.

luis_netops: NAT egress counts show ephemeral port usage at 78% on eu-west2-nat-1, CPU normal. But inter-AZ routing queues show bursts and interface errors on eni-azc-12. Running `tcptraceroute` and `mtr` to verify.

ryan_runtime: streaming runtime traces show many `send()` syscalls blocked >200ms waiting on socket. KV cache hits unchanged. This looks network-path related, not model runtime.

metrics-bot: p95: 820ms -> 1.1s (elevated), p99: 3.4s -> 4.1s across streaming endpoints. Error rate (stream disconnects) increased from 0.1% -> 6.2%. Request volume steady.

tim_oncall: action plan: 1) pin streaming traffic to same-AZ instances for a subset (canary) to test cross-zone hypothesis 2) fail open to stateless fallback model (smaller variant) for affected customers 3) open handoff if needed. executing 1 now: applying routing policy to prefer local-az targets for 5% traffic using `rb-policy set --tag prefer-local-az --pct 5 /v1/stream`.

deploy-bot: rollout started: rb-policy change applied to 5% traffic.

asha_sre: tcpdump from a affected node (excerpt):
```
15:23:08.123456 IP x.x.x.x.443 > y.y.y.y.51754: Flags [S.], seq 12345, ack 67890, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 654321], length 0
15:23:08.324789 IP x.x.x.x.443 > y.y.y.y.51754: Flags [S.], seq 12345, ack 67890, ... retransmit
```
Multiple SYN retransmits, handshake RTT ballooning 200->1500ms.

luis_netops: I see cross-zone interface errors on az-b -> az-c path around 15:22. Opening cloud provider support case. Also will try to shift route via az-a by updating route table for a small subset.

maria_support: Notifying affected customers with ETA 15-30m and mitigation steps; offering status updates.

tim_oncall: Canary to same-AZ reduced p99 for that shard to ~480ms, streaming disconnects dropped to 0.7% for canary slice. So this confirms cross-zone path degraded.

ryan_runtime: Good. As immediate mitigation, we can expand prefer-local-az to 30% traffic for streaming endpoints to reduce user impact while netops works on underlying path. Also preparing smaller model fallback for dedicated capacity customers (will require config push).

asha_sre: Running runbook step: `network-handshake-spike` — step 3 suggests scaling NAT or switching to regional egress. We can spin up additional NAT instances and drain connections from the affected NAT. Starting NAT scale now.

luis_netops: NAT scale initiated. Also deploying temporary iptables qdisc adjustments on affected hosts to increase socket backlog and lower SYN retries: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=4096`. Pushing now to az-c.

metrics-bot: After policies + NAT scale: p99 dropped from 3.4s -> 820ms cluster-wide, streaming disconnects from 6.2% -> 1.4%. Canary (same-AZ) stable at 470ms.

maria_support: customers notified of partial mitigation. Requesting concise summary for CSMs to send to enterprise customers.

tim_oncall: Summary for CSMs: "We observed cross-AZ networking instability causing elevated TLS handshake latency and packet retransmits, leading to streaming stalls for a subset of requests. Mitigations applied: local-AZ routing canary and NAT scaling. We're working with cloud provider to remediate inter-AZ path. Continued monitoring; follow-up incident report will include root cause and timeline."

asha_sre: opening incident page and will attach timeline + packet captures. Assigning Severity: Sev2 (customer impact, partial mitigation in progress).

luis_netops: cloud case opened (#CLOUD-99821). Provider reports congested leaf switch fabric in az-c; they are migrating flows and applying micro-patches. They estimate 45-90m to full stabilization.

ryan_runtime: Preparing durable fallback plan: 1) auto-fallback to non-streaming short-poll for affected customers if streaming disconnect rate exceeds 5% for 10m 2) auto-redirect to same-AZ endpoints for session stickiness. Will open PR for rollout config.

tim_oncall: Handing off to night shift oncall @asha_sre in 30m. If the cross-AZ path doesn't clear in that window escalate to Enginfra lead. I'll update the incident page and leave open.

asha_sre: Acknowledged. I'll take over monitoring, continue NAT/drain actions, and coordinate with cloud provider. If we see packet loss >2% again, we'll move to full regional egress routing.

maria_support: Logged customer impact notes and updated TKT-4821/TKT-4822. Will post a public status update after we confirm no new regressions.

metrics-bot: final note in thread: p99 now 750ms, streaming disconnect 0.9% (still above target). continuing to watch.

tim_oncall: leaving handoff: incident state=mitigated -> partial; next steps pinned in incident doc. Oncall out. :thumbsup:

asha_sre: taking over. Will update thread with any provider ETA changes or if we need further mitigations.

(End of thread)
